newsitem.title: TAIWAN: HK Telecom loses Taiwan mobile bidding.
newsitem.headline: HK Telecom loses Taiwan mobile bidding.

text.p: HongKong Telecom left empty-handed on Monday after a fierce bidding war for eight Taiwan mobile phone franchises amid reports that Taipei was blocking its bid due to its shareholder base in rival China.
Vice-Minister Mao Chih-kuo of the Ministry of Transport and Communications said consideration of Hongkong Telecom's mainland Chinese ownership was a factor but not a decisive one.

"We did discuss this question but that is not a special reason for which the company did not get a licence," Mao told reporters at a news conference after the winners of eight lucrative mobile franchises were announced.

Hong Kong newspapers in early January quoted an unnamed Taiwan telecom official as saying Hongkong Telecom was being blocked in the bidding because it is owned in part by one of communist China's leading state conglomerates.

Hong Kong-listed CITIC Pacific Ltd, controlled by Beijing's main overseas trade and investment arm, China International Trust and Investment Corp, or CITIC, holds about eight percent of Hongkong Telecom.
Hongkong Telecom holds a 15 percent interest in Taiwan's Taishin Telecom Corp, who bid for a Taiwan mobile franchise was rejected on Monday.

Taiwan has been estranged from the communist mainland since a civil war split them in 1949 and still bans official contacts with China's government, although pressure is mounting to allow direct transport, communications and trade.
